clue.text: Move on swine, back to front

indicators.note: the letter at the back of the word for swine is carried round to the front

parts.note: hogs are swine

explanation.surface: An instruction to drive pigs along, telling the herd to turn round.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the final S of HOGS to the start gives SHOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Shog is a dialect and archaic verb meaning to jog along or move off.

clue.text: Fun time for broads in nighties, secretive about brown character (12, two words)

definitions.text: Fun time for broads in nighties

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the secretive word goes round the rest

parts.note: sly means secretive, furtive
umber is a brown earth pigment
an actor's character is a part

explanation.surface: Pyjama-clad women having a good time, while someone sly takes an interest in a brown-skinned figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broads' is American slang for women; 'character' is a role, not a letter or a personality.
explanation.definitionFit: A slumber party is a sleepover where friends in nightclothes stay up late having fun.

clue.text: Willing to try

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an adjective for someone ready to tackle things, as in a plucky hero
second meaning: a verb phrase for making an attempt

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase, but splits into an adjective and a verb. A have-a-go hero, in British usage, is a bystander who tackles a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated adjective describes a person game for anything, while the phrase itself means to make an attempt.

clue.text: Duck young lady's stuffed with the French mushroom

indicators.note: something stuffed with a filling holds it inside, so the duck goes into the young lady

parts.note: a girl is a young lady
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, O
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A recipe: a girl's duck, stuffed with mushroom the French way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird to be stuffed; it is nought, the thing put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A girolle is a chanterelle, an edible yellow woodland mushroom.

clue.text: Bundle of firewood to intertwine with bits of corded hemp

parts.note: to knit is to intertwine yarn

indicators.note: bits of words here are just their opening letters

parts.note: the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Firewood bundled together and tied with hemp cord.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitch is a dialect word for a bundle of sticks or firewood tied together.

clue.text: From below, cuts off seat for the vicar?

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from below means reading the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: to elide is to cut off a sound or a part

explanation.surface: Someone sawing through the legs of the vicar's chair from underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a sedile seats clergy in general, not only a vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedile is one of the stone seats in a church chancel set aside for the officiating clergy.

clue.text: Timbers cut short

indicators.note: to cut a word is to trim off its final letter

parts.note: short in the sense of scanty, in limited supply

explanation.surface: Timber, perhaps for a building, sawn down to shorter lengths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' reads as one phrase meaning trimmed, but 'short' is SPARSE, and 'cut' docks its final E to leave SPARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spars are stout poles of wood, such as masts and booms on a ship, so they are timbers.

clue.text: Page appearing ahead of court official once? This may have been part of evidence

definitions.text: This may have been part of evidence

indicators.note: one thing appearing ahead of another is placed before it in the word

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page
a reeve was a medieval official presiding over a manor court or shire

explanation.surface: A young court page walks in front of an official, in a scene from an old trial.
explanation.walkthrough: Preeve is an obsolete spelling of proof, and proof is part of evidence; 'may have been' marks it as old.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof, of which preeve is an old form, is the part of evidence that establishes a fact.

clue.text: A nameless eco-warrior, square?

indicators.note: less means without, and N stands for name, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
a Green is an environmental campaigner

explanation.surface: Calling a nameless environmental activist old-fashioned and conventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' looks like an insult for a dull person; it is the verb meaning to tally.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts that square agree with each other, so square means correspond or match.

clue.text: Cash that is kept in registers

indicators.note: something kept in a place is held within it

parts.note: a meter reads, or registers, a quantity
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Money stored in the shop's cash registers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Registers' suggests tills, which suits cash; it is the verb meaning shows a reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Readies is British slang for ready money, cash in hand.

clue.text: Laplanders ride around before noon

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for ride goes round the other piece

parts.note: to sit a horse is to ride it
a.m., ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: People of Lapland out on a morning ride.
explanation.walkthrough: Samit is the plural form the Sami of Lapland use for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sami are the indigenous people of Lapland, and Samit is their own plural for the people.

clue.text: Politico on the world stage moved by sane protests

indicators.note: letters that are moved are shifted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An international politician swayed by reasonable demonstrations.
explanation.definitionFit: A statesperson is a respected political leader, especially one active in world affairs.

clue.text: Typical of sea birds seen from a liner at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Gulls glimpsed by passengers aboard an ocean liner.
explanation.definitionFit: Larine is the adjective for gulls, from Latin larus, a gull, which are the typical sea birds.

clue.text: Syrup? Coated in gum it makes you stuff a stomach!

parts.words: Coated in gum it makes you stuff a stomach
parts.note: surface reading: a sweet syrup thickened with gum is so rich it makes you overeat; setter's reading: wrap the syrup's name in G...UM and the result reads as a phrase meaning stuff a tummy

explanation.surface: A sticky syrup that, once thickened with gum, makes you overeat.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: put the answer inside GUM and you get G-ORGEAT-UM, read as 'gorge a tum', which is the clue's 'stuff a stomach'.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgeat is a sweet almond-flavoured syrup used in cocktails such as the mai tai.

clue.text: I pulled out of dodgy marriage bid — does it show bids on big screen?

definitions.text: does it show bids on big screen?

indicators.note: dodgy means unsound or shaky, so the remaining letters are rearranged
one who pulls out of something leaves it, so that letter is withdrawn from the phrase

parts.note: the letter to be taken away
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suspicious proposal of marriage, from which the speaker has withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one I from MARRIAGE BID and rearrange the ten letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridgerama is a large display board on which audiences at bridge tournaments follow the bidding and play.

clue.text: Resident alien bottles expression of joy? That's understating things

indicators.note: to bottle something is to shut it up inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a metic was a resident alien in an ancient Greek city
io is a Greek cry of triumph or joy

explanation.surface: A foreign resident suppressing their delight, which is putting it mildly.
explanation.walkthrough: A metic was a foreigner living with limited rights in an ancient Greek city; io is the Greek shout of triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: Meiosis in rhetoric is deliberate understatement, and meiotic is its adjective.

clue.text: What indicates first signs of baby asking, 'Where's lunch?'?

definitions.text: What indicates first signs of baby asking, 'Where's lunch?'?

indicators.note: the first signs of words are their opening letters

parts.note: initials of the four words

explanation.surface: How you can tell an infant is hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the initials, and a hungry baby's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A bawl is a loud cry, the way a hungry baby demands its feed.

clue.text: One of the pitchblendes, mostly uniform in name

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: to cite is to name or mention

indicators.note: mostly means all but a bit, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: level means even, uniform

explanation.surface: A uranium ore whose name is almost uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like the military letter U; here it means even or flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleveite is a variety of uraninite, the uranium mineral also called pitchblende, named after the chemist Cleve.

clue.text: One championing cause who's position in age-old festival

indicators.note: the position word is put in the festival word

parts.note: an ale was an old village festival where ale was drunk, as in church-ale
a post is a position or job

explanation.surface: A campaigner who has a role in an ancient celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Ale as a festival is an old sense, which is why the clue says age-old.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a leading advocate of a cause, by extension from the first followers of Jesus.

clue.text: Cardinal maybe sneers nastily being present

parts.note: HE, His Eminence, is a cardinal's title

indicators.note: done nastily, the letters are knocked about and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A churchman who looks down on those around him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' tempts a solver towards a number or a bird; it is the title His Eminence.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereness is the state of being here, that is, of being present.

clue.text: Web confused, enthralled by Orcadian dialect that's very young

indicators.note: one held enthralled by another is captured within it

parts.note: Norn was the Norse language once spoken in Orkney and Shetland

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by the internet, captivated instead by an old island tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Orcadian means from Orkney, the islands off northern Scotland, whose old Norse speech was Norn.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn is a baby only just born, as young as it is possible to be.

clue.text: Weeds economise when exercising (no MO turned up)

indicators.note: exercising puts the letters through their paces, moving them around
in a down clue, turned up means read upwards, backwards
no means without, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; once turned it matches two letters in the middle of the first word

explanation.surface: Someone saving money on a fitness routine, with no modus operandi.
explanation.walkthrough: MO reversed is OM; ECONOMISE without OM leaves ECONISE to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Senecio is the large plant genus that includes ragwort and groundsel, both common weeds.

clue.text: Waddy's wild? Dimwit missing rain in part

indicators.note: the shortened word is placed in the other one

parts.note: a part in a play is a role

indicators.note: something missing a thing goes without it

parts.note: a peabrain is a stupid person
taken as written; these letters leave

explanation.surface: An Aboriginal club runs amok while a fool misses out on rain somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: A waddy is an Aboriginal war club, which points to Australia, where ropeable is slang for furious. PEABRAIN minus RAIN is PEAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropeable is Australian slang for angry enough to need roping in, so wild with rage.

clue.text: What matador waves at bull, tail to head, displaying charm

indicators.note: the tail letter of the cloth's name is carried up to the head of the word

parts.note: the muleta is the red cloth a matador waves

explanation.surface: A bullfighter's cape-work at its most charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail to head' could describe the bull itself; it moves the final A to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn to ward off evil.

clue.text: Like some caterpillars, dead, if once trapped?

indicators.note: something trapped is held inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: the late means the dead
an is an archaic word for if

explanation.surface: Caterpillars that would die if they were ever caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead' looks like the fate of the trapped caterpillar; it is the word for the deceased that holds the old 'if'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanate means woolly, covered in fine hairs, as many caterpillars are.

clue.text: Purification vessel as standard inverted, until brought in

indicators.note: something brought in is placed inside the other word
turned upside down in a down entry, the word reads backwards

parts.note: a rule is a standard to judge by
to means until, as in from nine to five

explanation.surface: A laboratory flask held upside down as the normal practice, until something is added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As standard' reads as one phrase meaning routinely; 'as' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An elutor is a vessel used for elution, washing a substance out to purify it, as in sugar refining.

clue.text: Introductory old English mass in set of three

indicators.note: these pieces go in the word for the set of three

parts.note: a prial, from pair royal, is three cards of the same rank
OE is the abbreviation for Old English
m is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: An old English mass introduced as one of a trio of services.
explanation.walkthrough: A prial, short for pair royal, is a card-game term for three of a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A proem is a preface, so proemial means prefatory, serving as an introduction.

clue.text: Vain flappers share jumps

indicators.note: letters that jump leap about out of their places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Conceited young flappers in the twenties dividing their dance steps between them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vain flappers' looks like 1920s party girls; it means wings that flap in vain.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheas are large flightless South American birds, so their wings flap to no purpose.

clue.text: Praise Cockney magician, limp?

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops an initial H, so each word loses it

parts.note: a hex is a witch or wizard, as well as a spell
to halt is to limp, as in the halt and the lame

explanation.surface: Applauding an East End conjuror whose act has gone a bit floppy.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class London accent that drops the H at the start of words, which applies to both.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt someone is to praise them highly or glorify them.

clue.text: Decline once again, end brought forward

indicators.note: the letter at the end is moved to the front of the word

parts.note: anew means once again, afresh

explanation.surface: Turning something down a second time, the conclusion moved earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline once' looks like a single phrase; the definition is just 'Decline'.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon wanes as it shrinks, and to wane is to decline in strength or size.

clue.text: Books in nurse (ill), device to reduce shocks in US

definitions.text: device to reduce shocks in US

indicators.note: the books go in the other word
an ill nurse is out of sorts, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
B is book, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Reading matter for a sick nurse, alongside a gadget against electric shocks in America.
explanation.walkthrough: In American usage a snubber is a shock absorber on a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A snubber is a device that damps sudden jolts, and Americans use the word for a car's shock absorber.

clue.text: Not one to turn the other cheek? Round One anon, in comeback

definitions.text: Not one to turn the other cheek?

indicators.note: a comeback runs backwards, so the whole string is read from the end

parts.note: a rota is a round of duties
Roman numeral one
anon means soon, later

explanation.surface: A boxer who will not take punishment meekly, promising to hit back in round one before long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round One' reads as a boxing round; the words split into a rota, the numeral I and LATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning the other cheek means accepting injury without revenge; a retaliator always strikes back.

clue.text: New year festival with everything stored inside loft

indicators.note: something stored inside is kept within the other word

parts.note: Tet is the Vietnamese new year festival
all means everything

explanation.surface: New year celebrations, with everything packed away in the attic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loft' could be a verb for hitting high; it is the attic.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallet is a West Country dialect word for a hayloft or attic over a stable.

clue.text: US gangster brought back corruption and almost total mayhem

indicators.note: brought back means returned, read in the other direction

parts.note: rot is moral decay

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: a riot is total disorder

explanation.surface: An American mobster returned to a life of crime and near-total chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnny Torrio was the Chicago gang boss who brought in Al Capone.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrio ran Chicago's bootlegging gang in the Prohibition era before handing it to Capone.

clue.text: Fierce argument in ring after mishandled test

indicators.note: the ring comes after the other piece
something mishandled is bungled and so jumbled up

parts.note: taken as written
a ring is O-shaped

explanation.surface: A heated row in the boxing ring after a botched drugs test.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief fierce fight or argument.

clue.text: Culminating point? It was high on screen

definitions.meaning: first meaning: midday, when the sun culminates at its highest
second meaning: the time of day in the title of a 1952 western film

explanation.walkthrough: High Noon is the 1952 Gary Cooper western; the question mark marks the sun's culmination at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is when the sun reaches its highest point, and High Noon is a classic western's title.
